'''Jason Victor Smith''' (born March 2, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played twelve seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]]. He played college basketball for the [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State Rams]] before being selected with the 20th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]].

==High school career==
Smith attended Platte Valley High School in [[Kersey, Colorado]] where he was regarded as the state's premier prep player during his senior season in 2003–04. He was a two-time state player of the year, was named to the All-Colorado team as a junior and senior, was a three-year letterwinner and starter for the Broncos, was named to all-conference and all-state teams three times, and was selected as most outstanding player in state Class 3A tournament as a senior.<ref name=bio>{{Cite web |url=http://www.csurams.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jason_smith_226193.html |title=Jason Smith Bio |access-date=March 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150405180107/http://www.csurams.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jason_smith_226193.html |archive-date=April 5, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]] in 2004–05, Smith was named the Mountain West Freshman of the Year and earned all-MWC honorable mention honors. In 26 games (11 starts), he averaged 10.5 points on 55.4 percent shooting (103-of-186) with 5.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.4 blocked shots in 24.4 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

As a sophomore in 2005–06, Smith played in and started all 31 games for the Rams, and the season's end, he earned first-team All-Mountain West and second-team NABC all-district honors. On the season, he averaged 16.2 points on 51.7 percent shooting (178-of-344) with 7.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.1 blocked shots in 28.7 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

As a junior in 2006–07, Smith earned first-team All-Mountain West honors for a second straight year after he led the MWC in rebounding (10.1 rpg, ranked ninth nationally) and ranked sixth in scoring (16.8 ppg).<ref name=prospect>[http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/JasonSmith.html Prospect Profile: Jason Smith]</ref>

On April 3, 2007, Smith declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.csurams.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040307aaa.html |title=SMITH TO DECLARE FOR THE NBA DRAFT |access-date=March 22, 2015 |archive-date=April 5, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150405194634/http://www.csurams.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/040307aaa.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2824121 Smith, 7-foot junior, declares for NBA draft]</ref> He left Colorado State ranking ninth on the school's all-time leading scoring list with 1,281 points. He also ranked sixth in rebounds (683) and fifth in blocked shots (149), while his 24 career double-doubles was the second-most in school history.<ref name="prospect" />

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia 76ers (2007–2010)===
[[File:Jasonsmithsixers_cropped.JPG|thumb|right|upright|Smith with the 76ers in December 2007]]
Smith was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] with the 20th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]], but was later traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on draft night. As a rookie with the 76ers, Smith averaged 4.5 points and 3.0 rebounds in 76 games. In August 2008, he tore the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3525461|title=76ers C Smith, ex-Colorado State player, tears ACL|work=ESPN.com|date=August 8, 2008|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> He subsequently missed the entire 2008–09 season. Smith returned to action in 2009–10, playing in 56 games and averaging 3.4 points and 2.4 rebounds per game.

===New Orleans Hornets/Pelicans (2010–2014)===
On September 23, 2010, Smith was traded, along with [[Willie Green]], to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in exchange for [[Darius Songaila]] and [[Craig Brackins]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5607517|title=Rookie Craig Brackins traded to 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=September 23, 2010|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> On February 1, 2011, he scored a career-high 20 points in a 97–89 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310201003|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209124209/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310201003|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2018|title=Jason Smith scores 20 in rare start to lead Hornets past road-weary Wizards|work=ESPN.com|date=February 1, 2011|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> In 77 games, he averaged 4.3 points and 3.1 rebounds per game.

On December 17, 2011, Smith re-signed with the Hornets to a three-year, $7.5 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_resign_jason_smith_2011_12_17.html|title=Hornets Re-Sign Jason Smith|work=NBA.com|date=December 17, 2011|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7361143/new-orleans-hornets-re-sign-reserve-seven-foot-forward-jason-smith|title=Hornets re-sign Jason Smith|work=ESPN.com|date=December 16, 2011|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> He missed over a month of action between February 4 and March 17 due to a concussion suffered on February 4 against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2012/03/hornets_forward_smith_still_ex.html|title=New Orleans Hornets forward Jason Smith still experiencing concussion symptoms|work=NOLA.com|date=March 3, 2012|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/smithja02/gamelog/2012/|title=Jason Smith 2011-12 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> On April 7, 2012, he scored a career-high 26 points in a 99–90 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320407003|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209165249/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320407003|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2018|title=Jason Smith's career game lets Hornets down Wolves|work=ESPN.com|date=April 7, 2012|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> He appeared in 40 games and made 29 starts while averaging a career-high 9.9 points and 4.9 rebounds in the [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout]]-shortened 2011–12 season.

Smith managed just 51 games in 2012–13 due to a right [[Glenoid labrum|labrum]] injury that forced him to miss seven games in December.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2012/12/new_orleans_hornets_forward_ja_13.html|title=New Orleans Hornets forward Jason Smith to miss at least two weeks with shoulder injury|last=Smith|first=Jimmy|date=December 14, 2012|website=NOLA|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> Smith later missed the final 24 games of the season after having season-ending surgery to repair it.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nola.com/pelicans/index.ssf/2014/02/new_orleans_pelicans_jason_smi_2.html|title=New Orleans Pelicans' Jason Smith out for remainder of season after undergoing knee surgery last week: notebook|last=Reid|first=John|date=February 4, 2014|website=NOLA|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> In April 2013, the Hornets were renamed the Pelicans.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9187070/new-orleans-hornets-announce-name-change-pelicans-official|title=Hornet free: New Orleans officially the Pelicans|date=April 18, 2013|website=ESPN|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref>

In 2013–14, Smith was limited to 31 games due to season-ending knee injury in January 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/2013-14-season-review-jason-smith|title=2013-14 Season In Review: Jason Smith {{!}} New Orleans Pelicans|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2014–2015)===
On July 18, 2014, Smith signed a one-year, $3.3 million contract with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/11220548/jason-smith-new-york-knicks-reach-1-year-33-million-deal|title=Knicks sign F/C Smith to 1-year, $3.3M deal|last=Begley|first=Ian|date=July 15, 2014|website=ESPN|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> On February 7, 2015, Smith grabbed a season-high 13 rebounds against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400579052|title=Warriors vs. Knicks - Box Score - February 7, 2015 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> On February 11, 2015, Smith scored a season-high 25 points on 10-of-16 shooting in an 89–83 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400579080|title=Vucevic scores 26 to help Magic hold off Knicks 89-83|date=February 11, 2015|website=ESPN.com|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> He appeared in all 82 games for the first time in his career and made a career-high 31 starts.

===Orlando Magic (2015–2016)===
On July 14, 2015, Smith signed a one-year, $4.5 million contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13216739/jason-smith-sign-orlando-magic|title=Magic reach one-year deal with Jason Smith|last=Begley|first=Ian|date=July 7, 2015|website=ESPN|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> On March 15, 2016, he set season highs with 25 points and 13 rebounds in a 116–110 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160315/DENORL/gameinfo.html|title=Fournier, Smith help Magic hold off Nuggets, 116-110|date=March 15, 2016|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2016–2018)===
[[File:Jason Smith (50595921577).jpg|thumb|Jason Smith (2018)]]
On July 7, 2016, Smith signed a three-year, $16 million contract to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/07/07/wizards-sign-free-agents-mahinmi-nicholson-smith|title=Wizards Sign Free Agents Mahinmi, Nicholson & Smith|work=MonumentalSportsNetwork.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016|archive-date=August 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817062243/https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/07/07/wizards-sign-free-agents-mahinmi-nicholson-smith|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wizards-insider/wp/2016/07/05/wizards-agree-to-three-year-deal-with-veteran-big-man-jason-smith/|title=Wizards agree to three-year deal with veteran big man Jason Smith|last=Bontemps|first=Tim|date=July 5, 2016|website=Wizards Insider|publisher=Washington Post|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> He scored a season-high 17 points three times during the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/smithja02/gamelog/2017/|title=Jason Smith 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> The 2017–18 season saw Smith appear in just 33 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/smithja02/gamelog/2018/|title=Jason Smith 2017-18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 7, 2018}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2018–2019)===
On December 7, 2018, Smith was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in a five-player, three-team deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bucks Acquire George Hill and Jason Smith in a Three-Team Deal With Cleveland and Washington|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-george-hill-and-jason-smith-three-team-deal-cleveland-and-washington|access-date=December 8, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=December 7, 2018}}</ref>

===Return to New Orleans (2019)===
On February 7, 2019, Smith was acquired by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in a three-team trade involving the Bucks and [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-acquire-stanley-johnson-jason-smith|title=Pelicans acquire Stanley Johnson, Jason Smith|work=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2019|access-date=February 7, 2019}}</ref> On March 20, 2019, he was waived by the Pelicans after appearing in two games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-claim-christian-wood-waivers|title=Pelicans claim Christian Wood off waivers|work=NBA.com|date=March 20, 2019|access-date=March 20, 2019}}</ref>
